newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher for fourth day in row.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher for fourth day in row.

text.p: Bombay shares rallied at close on Thursday after opening mixed and took the market's winning streak to four straight days this week, dealers said.
Some local fund buying aided by rumours that former finance minister Manmohan Singh might take over as chief of the Congress parliamentary party helped market sentiment.
The Press Trust of India reported that former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao stepped down from his last post as chief of the Congress party's parliamentary delegation.
"The rumour about Rao was one of the reasons behind the rally..," said chief dealer Ketan Jhaveri at Kotak Securities.
"Mr Rao submitted his resignation moments before the 1600 hrs (1030 GMT) deadline set by the Congress president, Mr Sitaram Kesri, for him to resign," PTI said.
Kesri had set the deadline after an unprecedented resolution by leaders of the parliamentary delegation on Wednesday, which demanded that Rao give up his post for the sake of party unity.
A spate of corruption allegations forced him to step down as Congress president in September.
"This (Rao's resignation) might be reflected in tomorrow's prices...in anticipation of favourable developments," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at broker Pashupati Advani.
Scattered buying by the Unit Trust of India, the country's biggest mutual fund, in blue-chip shares such as Hind Lever and Bajaj Auto pepped market sentiment, participants said.
"The downward risk in prices has been reduced. People have started talking about bottom levels," said Kotak's Jhaveri.

The Bombay Stock Exchange top index ended 34.37 points or 1.15 percent up at provisional 3,035.61, the day's high. The National Stock Exchange index rose 4.33 points or 0.50 percent to a provisional 864.33.
SBI added 2.75 rupees to 221.25, Reliance 3.0 to 197.25, ACC 25.50 to 1,155, TISCO 2.0 to 161 and Hind Lever 10.5 to 806.75.
